_README: Time-boxed credential exceptions. Checked by scripts/check-storage-isolation.js, which is
part of preflight, so an expired exception turns the build red rather than quietly persisting.
An exception is a decision with an end date. Without enforcement the end date is a sentiment:
the 90-day window is only real if something fails on day 91. That something is this file.

exceptions.what: Railway holds long-lived static AWS access keys for PRPA document storage, in sealed variables
why: Railway documents no workload-identity or OIDC mechanism that an AWS IAM role could trust.
Its only OIDC is inbound dashboard SSO; secrets reach a service solely as environment
variables. A Railway service therefore cannot call sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, because
it has no web identity to present. Long-lived keys are the only documented path.
reassess_what: The AWS-hosted storage broker (option B in the ruling-17 return): a component on AWS
holding S3/KMS access via an IAM role, which Railway calls with a broker token. It does
not remove a long-lived shared secret; it narrows what one can do. Reassess against the
named triggers: a second consumer of the document store, materially higher document
volume or sensitivity, or an external requirement forbidding static cloud credentials on
compensating_controls: Least-privilege IAM policy scoped to the prpa/ prefix and one KMS key
No s3:DeleteObject and no bucket- or key-administration actions
Separate development identity, bucket and key, with explicit cross-environment Deny
Bucket policy denying every principal except the one identity and the scanner role
Railway sealed variables: not retrievable via UI or API, and not copied into PR or
duplicated environments, so a duplicated environment cannot inherit the production key
Application-level refusal to start when the environment and the bucket disagree

rotation.iam_access_keys: quarterly, manual — Railway documents no rotation mechanism; tracked separately from KMS per ruling 18 item 4

kms_rotation.decision: annual automatic rotation enabled on both customer-managed keys
cost_consequence: AWS bills the first and second rotation of key material at $1/month each and caps there:
'This price increase is capped at the second rotation, and any subsequent rotations will
not be billed.' So per key: $1 now, $2 after 2027-11-06, $3 after 2028-11-05, and $3
thereafter. For both keys the steady state is $6/month, reached 2028-11-05.
Deliberately accepted: $4/month more than the unrotated figure, against a total that stays
under $16/month even at a hundred times the assumed document volume.
kms_rotation.kept_separate_from: IAM access-key rotation, per ruling 18 item 4 — the two have different mechanisms, different failure modes, and different blast radius
